chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Idrees al-Qummi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands the Angel of Death, so he returns the soul of the Believer to ease it upon him, and extracts it from the best of its states. The people say, 'Death was severe upon so-and-so,' but that is an easing from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon him. And He says: It is turned away from him (the severity) if he is one upon whom Allah is pleased, or one whom Allah loves his affair, that He does not pull the pull with the like of the skewer of wet wool. So the people say, 'Allah has eased death for so-and-so.'
ai.seo_question: How does Allah ease the death of a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the theological concept of *Taysir* (easing) versus *Tashdid* (hardening) in death, illustrating how divine mercy can manifest as perceived severity for the believer, while divine displeasure results in a gentle exit for the righteous. The hadith employs a vivid metaphor of the 'wet wool' (*al-saff al-mablul*) to describe the intense, painful extraction for those Allah loves, contrasting it with the ease granted to others, a nuance often discussed in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the varying states of the soul at death. This duality underscores the Shia understanding that the external appearance of death does not always reflect the internal spiritual reality or divine decree.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Idrees Al Qummy who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Commands the Angel of death, so he returns the soul of the Believer in order to ease upon him, and extracts it from the best of its modes’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Idris af-Qummiy who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, commands the angel of death to return the soul of a believing person, make it easy for him, and then take it out in the most comfortable way. People then say, “It (dying) was very difficult for so and so.” In fact it is the way Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, provides him comfort.’ He then said, ‘It (comfort) is denied him if he is of those with whom Allah is angry, or Allah dislikes him. He commands him (the angel) to pull out his soul just as frying-bar is pulled out of wool soaked in water and people say, “Allah has made dying very easy for him.’””
